text:
Sampled ranking can change model ordering: [Krichene–Rendle](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/651) demonstrate inconsistency, and [RecSys 2025 research](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) examines sampling fidelity and exposure bias. Keep the pinned 99-negative macro HR@10 as the selection criterion. Proposed uncertainty analysis: if host outputs include per-user hits, bootstrap paired model differences within each category, then average the four category differences. Aggregate scores alone cannot recover paired uncertainty. These intervals describe validation-user variability conditional on fixed candidates, not training or candidate-sampling variability.

[2024 negative-sampling experiments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) show that average accuracy can hide head/mid/tail disparities. Proposed audit without pretrained weights: fit TF-IDF on permitted titles/descriptions; retrieve lexically similar unseen items and inspect where the single GRU4Rec model ranks them against validation positives. Record positive rank, score margin, distractor overlap, and explicit attribute conflicts. Treat these as potentially relevant alternatives, not confirmed negatives. Report full-catalog and lexical-hard-pool diagnostics separately from pinned HR@10; use no auxiliary scores in prediction. Missing interaction is not evidence of dislike.

A [2024 qualitative Netflix study](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12646-024-00807-0) connects dissatisfaction with repetition and limited diversity. Proposed rubric for twenty users’ feedback: broad-topic relevance, functional fit, slate redundancy, historical repetition, and explicit rejection reason; attach an evidence excerpt and supported/contradicted/unknown status. Mark ownership and compatibility unknown unless explicitly established; interaction does not establish ownership. Measure redundancy using duplicate titles and pairwise lexical similarity. Keep simulator statements separate from verified facts, permit multiple rejection labels, and report user-level counts plus annotation disagreements. Five users per category support exploratory diagnosis, not reliable population estimates.
